solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Chat with me and Mark about union negotiator (10)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in scattered around: the letters are moved about

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A trade union's negotiator is invited in for a chat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'and' simply gather the three words into one pile of fodder; the union is a marriage, not a trade union.
annotation.definitionFit: A matchmaker brokers a union between two people, a marriage.

entries.clue: Spies entertaining cryptic clue for “particles” (9)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain guests is to hold them inside
indicatorNotes.cryptic: a cryptic version of a word is a scrambled one

blocks.note: moles are spies planted inside an organisation
CLUE rearranged, placed inside MOLE…S

annotation.surface: Spies are handed a coded clue whose answer is "particles".
annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'cryptic clue' looks like crossword jargon but is an anagram instruction plus its fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A scientific example of the definition: in chemistry these are the smallest units of a compound, the particles that bonded atoms form.

entries.clue: Drag queen hiding in shadow (5)

indicatorNotes.hiding in: the queen is hidden inside the shadow word

blocks.note: to tail someone is to shadow them
R = Regina, queen; goes inside T…AIL

annotation.surface: A drag queen lurks in the shadows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' is a single phrase in the surface, but the clue splits it: 'Drag' is the definition and 'queen' is R.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the verb sense of pulling something along behind you, as a bride's train sweeps the floor.

entries.clue: Lady in charge content to shout — big match nerves? (13)

indicatorNotes.content to: the content of a word is what is inside it, dropping its outer letters

blocks.note: the inside of S-HOU-T
a semi-final, a big match
nerves = stress

annotation.surface: A woman in charge is happy just to shout her team on through the tension of a big match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Content to shout' reads as 'happy to shout', but 'content' here is the noun: what the word SHOUT contains.
annotation.definitionFit: A housemistress is the teacher in charge of a boarding-school house.

entries.clue: Element of surprise ultimately lost by Wenger, football manager no longer in charge (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: points to the final letter of 'surprise'
indicatorNotes.lost by: that letter is taken away from the name
indicatorNotes.no longer: Wenger is a manager no longer, i.e. a former one

blocks.note: Arsène Wenger, former Arsenal manager, minus the E that ends 'surprise'
last letter of 'surprise', the letter removed
IC = in charge

annotation.surface: A newspaper story: the element of surprise is gone from a football manager who has left his job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Element of surprise' is a stock phrase, but 'Element' alone is the definition. Arsène Wenger managed Arsenal (a London football club) from 1996 to 2018.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this is element 33 on the periodic table, the poisoner's favourite.

entries.clue: European arranged to house pet for president (7)

indicatorNotes.to house: the second part holds the pet inside it

blocks.note: E = European
to run an event is to arrange it; past tense RAN
a pet dog, placed inside R…AN

annotation.surface: A European organises a home for a head of state's pet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' tempts as an anagram indicator, but no fodder of seven letters fits; it is RAN, as in 'ran the show'.
annotation.definitionFit: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is the president of Turkey.

entries.clue: Block return of large sum of money (4)

indicatorNotes.return of: to return is to go back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: pots of money = a large sum

annotation.surface: Someone is trying to stop a large payment being given back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pots' is informal British for a lot of money: 'pots of cash'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to block a move, a shot or a plan is to halt it.

entries.clue: Posed around clergyman’s house with a drink (6,3)

indicatorNotes.around: turned around, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a model sat, or posed, for the artist
a manse is a minister's house, especially in Scotland
kept as is

annotation.surface: Someone posed for photos near the vicar's house, drink in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is crossword slang for the sea, so a drink here is a whole sea, not a glass of something.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea, between Australia and New Zealand, is a stretch of 'the drink'.

entries.clue: Recipient of money agreed to cut exercises (5)

indicatorNotes.to cut: the word cuts into the other, landing inside it

blocks.note: PE = physical education, school exercises
aye = yes, agreed; goes inside P…E

annotation.surface: Someone who has been paid has agreed to do less exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the school gym lesson.
annotation.definitionFit: A payee is the person to whom money is paid.

entries.clue: Fever interrupts the French classes (7)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: the fever breaks into the middle of the French word

blocks.note: les = the (French plural)
ague is an old word for a malarial fever; goes inside LE…S

annotation.surface: An illness breaks out and disrupts French lessons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Classes' reads as school lessons, but it means grades of quality, as in 'not in the same league'.
annotation.definitionFit: Leagues are classes or levels of standing: 'out of his league'.

entries.clue: Extremely dirty and unpleasant old soap (7)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: takes the extremes, first and last letters, of the next word

blocks.note: outer letters of DirtY
nasty = unpleasant

annotation.surface: A grumble about a filthy old bar of soap.
annotation.walkthrough: The soap is a soap opera: Dynasty was a 1980s American TV serial, not a cake of something dirty.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1980s American TV serial about the oil-rich Carrington family, a soap opera long off the air.

entries.clue: Crazy Horse entering Hell (6,7)

indicatorNotes.Crazy: crazy letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Crazy Horse, the Lakota war leader, goes to hell.
annotation.walkthrough: Crazy Horse was a Lakota chief, so the name looks like a unit, but 'Crazy' is the anagram instruction and 'entering' belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the lower regions were traditionally where the damned went; the phrase is also a coy term for the genitals.

entries.clue: Beware cuddling large bear (5)

indicatorNotes.cuddling: to cuddle something is to wrap your arms round it

blocks.note: cave! is Latin for 'beware', old school slang
L = large, placed inside CA…VE

annotation.surface: A warning not to hug a big bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb: to bear young. CAVE was a public-school warning cry that a teacher was coming.
annotation.definitionFit: Specialised sense: a cow giving birth is said to do this, matching 'bear' as in bear young.

entries.clue: Picked up chess piece, and something resembling it, in difficult situation (9)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear, so heard, not seen

blocks.note: the knight is a chess piece; NIGHT sounds the same
the knight is carved as a horse's head, so a mare resembles it

annotation.surface: Someone in a tight spot grabs a chess piece and a lookalike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the chess piece: a knight is shaped like a horse, hence MARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a bad dream extended to any ordeal, as in 'the traffic was a total ___'.

entries.clue: Cooler to not tell the truth before huge fraud, and more stupid (6,9)

blocks.note: to lie
a big con
denser = more stupid

annotation.surface: An accusation that someone who is chillier than the rest lies, cheats massively and is dim besides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a comparative adjective in line with 'more stupid', but it is a noun: a device that cools.
annotation.definitionFit: A Liebig condenser is a laboratory device that cools vapour back into liquid.

entries.clue: Court test cases dispatched, ignoring second demand (9)

indicatorNotes.cases: the test encases the court abbreviation

blocks.note: an exam is a test
CT = court, placed inside EXA…M
sent off = dispatched
S = second, dropped from SENT to leave ENT

annotation.surface: A judge's test cases are dealt with, skipping the second of them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like legal cases, but here it is a verb: the test encloses the court. Exactment is a rare word for a demand or exaction.
annotation.definitionFit: Rare Chambers word built from 'exact' (to require by force) plus -ment, the thing so required.

entries.clue: Shot her away from the coast, in part of Germany (9)

indicatorNotes.Shot: shot as in wrecked, broken into pieces

blocks.note: HER rearranged
inland = away from the coast

annotation.surface: Someone shot a woman well away from the shore somewhere in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as firing a gun, but it means ruined, jumbled; RHEINLAND is the German spelling of the Rhineland.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rheinland (Rhineland) is the region of western Germany along the Rhine.

entries.clue: Temporary hitch in the end admitted by celebrated coach scratching head (7,8)

indicatorNotes.admitted by: let in, so placed inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.scratching head: scratching off its head, the first letter

blocks.note: a star is celebrated
a term is an end or limit, as in terminus
a railway coach is a carriage; loses its first letter C to give ARRIAGE

annotation.surface: A top football coach suffers a short-lived setback at the end of the season.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' is the definition's pun: to get hitched is to marry. Using 'the end' for a limit of time, as in the term of a lease, is a stretch worth learning.
annotation.definitionFit: A starter marriage is a short first marriage ending in divorce, a temporary hitch.

entries.clue: Schedule includes a chicken for cooking? (7)

indicatorNotes.includes: the schedule has the A inside it

blocks.note: a roster is a duty schedule
placed inside RO…STER

annotation.surface: A kitchen timetable features a chicken for dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'for cooking' describes a roaster loosely: a bird raised to be roasted.
annotation.definitionFit: Specialised sense: poulterers grade birds by use, and this grade is sold to go in the oven; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

entries.clue: Referred every man dropping dead, at first (7)

indicatorNotes.dropping: in a down clue the letter drops from the top to the bottom
indicatorNotes.at first: names which D moves: the one at the start

blocks.note: all = every
a dude is a man; its first D drops to the bottom of this down entry, giving UDED
D = dead, naming the letter that moves; it is already counted in DUDE

annotation.surface: A report mentioned that everyone had died, early on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping dead' looks like a phrase about dying, but the D (dead) at the top of DUDE drops to the bottom of this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to refer to it indirectly.

entries.clue: With it starting late, perhaps March dance can encompass beginning of Easter (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.starting late: starts a letter late, so the first letter is lost
indicatorNotes.encompass: the two parts surround the letter between them

blocks.note: March is an example of a month; losing its first letter gives ONTH
first letter of Easter, held between ONTH and BALL
a ball is a formal dance

annotation.surface: A March dance runs late, but still covers the start of Easter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With it' reads as the start of the wordplay, but it is the definition: alert, up to date.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone with it is alert and competent, on the ball.
annotation.definitionNote: an adjectival phrase, as is the answer

entries.clue: Musk is old and miserable (5)

blocks.note: O = old
dour = gloomy, miserable

annotation.surface: A dig at a tech billionaire: he's old and grumpy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Musk' reads as Elon Musk, but it is musk the scent.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: musk is one particular scent, from the musk deer.

entries.clue: Pick up golf tip (5)

blocks.note: G = golf in the NATO alphabet
to tip over is to lean

annotation.surface: A golfer picks up a handy tip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as advice, but it is the verb: to tilt, lean.
annotation.definitionFit: To glean is to pick up or gather bit by bit.

entries.clue: Some paralegals lying about satellite (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the word's letters, not all
indicatorNotes.lying about: lying turned about, so read backwards

blocks.note: p-ARALE-gals

annotation.surface: Some paralegals are fibbing about a satellite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' reads as telling lies, but here it is positional: lying back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: Elara is one of Jupiter's moons, a natural satellite.

entries.clue: Cryptically, 2 Kings 6:29, for example, is in disorder (7)

indicatorNotes.Cryptically: tells the solver to read the example as a verse sitting in the Old Testament

blocks.note: chapter 6, verse 29 of 2 Kings is a verse
2 Kings is a book of the Old Testament, OT; the verse goes inside O…T

annotation.surface: A Bible reference is declared a mess.
annotation.walkthrough: The single example does double duty: the reference is a verse, and 2 Kings is a book of the Old Testament, so it sits inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Overset means upset, overturned, thrown into disorder.

entries.clue: Three-dimensional representation of moon in theatre (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the moon goes inside the theatre word

blocks.note: theatre as an art form = drama
Io is one of Jupiter's moons; goes inside D…RAMA

annotation.surface: A stage set shows a 3D model of the moon.
annotation.walkthrough: Io is a moon of Jupiter, the usual crossword moon.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a museum scene of models set against a painted backdrop gives exactly this effect of depth.

entries.clue: Pity husband after period of sexual excitement (4)

indicatorNotes.after: sends the husband second, placed after the rutting period

blocks.note: the rut is an animal's mating season
H = husband

annotation.surface: Feel sorry for the husband once the passion has worn off.
annotation.walkthrough: Ruth is an old word for pity; it survives in 'ruthless'.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaic word for compassion, still heard in its opposite 'ruthless'.

entries.clue: School members married wearing decorated fabric, helped by me? (10)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the bride; the answer is the 'me' who helps her

indicatorNotes.wearing: the letters are worn inside the fabric

blocks.note: braid is decorative trimming fabric
ides are fish, which swim in a school
M = married; IDES+M go inside BR…AID

annotation.surface: Pupils at a wedding in fancy clothes, assisted by the speaker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' reads as pupils, but it is a school of fish: an ide is a freshwater fish. The bride is the one 'helped by me', the bridesmaid.
annotation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid helps the bride, who is thus 'helped by me' from the bridesmaid's view.
